findings.text: the eight open lobes are not one mechanism class. On the retained regenerated fixture, boundary_flux_at_admitted_saddle finds no stationary saddle cell for state ids 0, 1 (stationary_count 0; the value returned is the locator, i.e. the field's own flux at the carried-over X-point coordinate, -0.035581017 for state 0), so those states plus 2, 3, 5, 6 are the documented level-fallback class: the assembly is handed a level that is not the field's separatrix value and the axis-enclosing component comes back open with zero closed segments. States 4 and 13 are NOT that class: a stationary saddle cell is found and its polished value returned (level_equals_nearest_stationary true; saddle at (0.6605, -1.3391) m, 0.0376 m from the carried coordinate, value -0.058062563 for state 4; and (0.6085, -1.2884) m, 0.0402 m, -0.092267516 for state 13) and the assembly still fails, with cycle_component_count 1 and axis_enclosing_component_count 1 but closed_candidate_count 0 -- a closed cycle that is not the axis-enclosing component while the axis-enclosing one is open. Two of the eight therefore do demonstrate a tracer failure at a correctly posed level; six do not, because the level handed over was never the field's own saddle value. The successor needs both a fixture-provenance repair and a tracer node, not one of the two.

the follow-on misstates which quantity moved by 0.103 Wb. "the twenty state levels differ by up to 0.103 Wb" is not what was measured: the level deltas between the two fixtures are +0.022491 at state 0 falling monotonically to -0.001226 at state 19, a maximum magnitude of 0.0225 Wb, while 0.103 Wb is the maximum absolute difference of the psi arrays themselves (state 0). The sentence that follows, "the early indices read 0.024 Wb higher", is the true level figure. A successor sizing the level shift from the 0.103 figure would overstate it fourfold; the psi figure is separately true and should be stated as the field, not the level.

inside the regenerated fixture the recorded X-point flux does not belong to the field stored beside it. xpoint_flux_0 is -0.05807224693241642 while the stored psi_0 at the stored X-point coordinate (0.6522838260850017, -1.3338929313043535) is -0.035581016859262335, a 0.0225 Wb disagreement in one file; the stored value instead agrees to 2e-11 with the level the committed census measured on the OLD field for that state (-0.058072246912655). Any successor that reads xpoint_flux_i as this field's boundary flux, or that assumes the fixture's null metadata was re-solved with it, will inherit that disagreement -- and the null metadata is the input the whole level derivation turns on.

"axis and X-point positions agree to 1e-14" is loose for the last four states. Measured axis and X-point deltas between the two fixtures are 8e-16 to 1.4e-14 for state ids 0 to 15, then 4.2e-13 and 4.2e-13 (16, 17), 5.1e-10 and 5.0e-10 (18, 19). The conclusion the sentence supports -- that the nulls did not move while the field did -- is sound; the tolerance quoted is not the one measured.

status complete with a driving item half unlanded. The driving followup asked for panel-states.npz to be regenerated so the persisted fixture is no longer stale against the driver; the fixture was regenerated, found to redden test_persisted_state_closes_the_axis_enclosing_lobe at state ids 0 and 13, and deliberately not committed. The decision itself is right -- the alternative is a red gate and a census record at odds with itself -- and it is argued in the plan landing comment, the evidence anchor, blockers and follow_ons alike, with the evidence retained. Recording it: the node's terminal status is complete while one of four driving items has no landed deliverable in the repository, so a coordinator reading status alone will not see that the stale fixture survives this node.

justifications.durability: Five commits, each with a conventional subject and a body that states what moved and why; none carries an AI attribution or a plan or ticket identifier in a symbol, filename or comment. Work was committed incrementally rather than in one terminal sweep, the manifest carried the numbers before the final generation, and the run survived eleven resumes with the outcome intact. The measurement evidence is durable in the places a successor reads: the regenerated fixture, its census, the redrawn panel, both CPU receipts and the terminal raster under the reports fence, with a copy beside the run directory and an index in the node report. The one weak point is the same one goal_fidelity names: the refreshed fixture, which is the input the successor needs, exists only as an untracked copy under the reports fence and is not in version control, so it is one pruner away from being lost; the node says so and names the path, which is the most it can do without landing the fixture.
justifications.evidence: The strongest thing here is that the numbers reproduce. I re-ran the declared gate myself in one all_debug allocation at the merged head d4810d0e with JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu through /home/ITER/mcintos/Code/nova/.venv/bin/python and PYTHONPATH at the review worktree, never uv: tests/test_flux_surface_connectivity.py plus tests/test_separatrix_branches.py gave 34 passed in 113.23s with exit 0, and the twenty-state census over the committed fixture gave 0 of 20 failing, then the retained regenerated fixture gave 8 of 20 failing at exactly state ids 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 and 13 -- the node's count and the node's index set, reproduced from the retained fixture through the public entry points without a new solve. The CPU-provenance path is real: the retained receipt names scheduler.node 98dci4-clu-3142.iter.org, scheduler.partition all_debug, job 1273959, runtime.jax_platforms cpu, runtime.host and runtime.platform, and measurement_host_marker carrying the reason text; and the refusal is preserved in code for an unmarked run off the reservation (benchmarks/coil_edit_latency.py:188-197). The retention is complete: fixture, regenerated census, panel, both CPU receipts and the redrawn SVG all sit under the reports fence. Deductions: the mechanism is presented as one class when it is two (finding below), and two quantitative claims in the same follow-on paragraph do not survive measurement (findings below). A claim a successor will build on that misstates which quantity moved by 0.103 Wb is an evidence defect even though the run in which it was measured was sound.
justifications.fit: The node fits its plan section and did the right thing with what it found: it refused to make the branch green by landing a fixture that would redden test_persisted_state_closes_the_axis_enclosing_lobe, it kept the green census honest by preserving the field it was measured on, and it escalated the discrepancy into a named follow-on rather than normalising it away. That is the behaviour the evidence contract asks for. What does not fit is the shape of the escalation. Presented as one mechanism ("a tracer defect on the live field", "the edge-root bracket is complete for the field it was validated against and incomplete for the field the current equilibrium path produces"), the eight open lobes are two mechanisms: six states where no stationary saddle cell is found at all and the level handed to the assembly is the flux at a coordinate rather than the field's own saddle value, and two states that fail at the field's own polished saddle value. That distinction is exactly what the successor routes on -- a tracer defect or a fixture-provenance defect -- and the record blurs it. The follow-on is still the most valuable thing this node produced and it is stated with its evidence location, so the fit is good on intent and weaker on the one classification the successor must not get wrong.
justifications.goal_fidelity: Items (1) and (2) landed and are verified first-hand. (1): the committed docs/figures/forward-solve-api/coil-edit-nonconvergence/branch-terms.json now reads closed_candidate_count 1 at states 9, 10, 11, 12 (well_formed true, closed_segment_count 67, 67, 69, 69) and carries no state reading 0, so it no longer contradicts the record beside it; my own census over the same committed fixture through boundary_flux_at_admitted_saddle and assemble_separatrix_branches returns 0 of 20 failing, matching it. (2): benchmarks/coil_edit_latency.py:1588 names the reference orientation in the panel suptitle -- "upper-null state whose admitted saddle sits above its axis, while every ..." -- not only in the caption. Item (3) is named as not done with a verifiable reason: benchmarks/diiid_poloidal_figures.py imports matplotlib, numpy and nova.media.ink (lines 30-35) and no tracer, so the fix has nothing to propagate to, and the fence accepts a named not-done. Item (4) is half landed and this is the deduction: the code half is real and exercised (see evidence), but the driving followup asked for panel-states.npz to be regenerated so the persisted fixture is no longer stale against the driver, and that fixture is deliberately NOT committed, so the committed fixture is stale exactly as before and the census the plan carries still describes a field the current equilibrium path no longer produces. The node states this openly rather than disguising it, and its own status is complete with the deviation reported under follow_ons, which is the honest form; but the node's own contract read "SPEC exact" and one of the four driving items has an unlanded deliverable, so goal fidelity cannot be scored as met.
justifications.scope_discipline: All five commits touch only declared fence paths -- benchmarks/coil_edit_latency.py (df4791d1), docs/figures/forward-solve-api/coil-edit-nonconvergence/branch-terms.json (5738d3f7), docs/plans/forward-solve-api.html and docs/evidence/archive/forward-solve-api-landed.html (298bef8b, a0149cc8, 960c4864) -- and nothing in the concurrent-node lists (cank-receipt-repairs, cco-review-repairs, msc-newton-krylov-route-regression, sos-grid-route-order) is touched. The artifacts it had itself written were restored in the worktree rather than left as accidental dirt, and the worktree is clean at 960c4864. The regenerated fixture and receipts were written under the node's own reports fence, which is inside its declared scope. The only reservation is that a rewrite of a committed figure directory (restoring the panel and fixture to the state the committed census was measured on) is a mutation of published artifacts performed to keep the branch green against a field the branch no longer builds, which the node itself flags; that is a judgement call inside scope, not straying outside it.
